committees.name: Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee

dimensions.assessment: Affects drug manufacturers, packers, distributors, and importers operating in the U.S. market.
dimensions.evidence: No person shall introduce or deliver for introduction into interstate commerce any drug--(A) if it is an active pharmaceutical ingredient, unless the label... contain the name and place of business of the original manufacturer

dimensions.assessment: Establishes civil monetary penalties up to 25 percent of the total value of the drug product lot for noncompliance.
dimensions.evidence: Any person who fails to comply with the requirements of section 503(i) shall be subject to a civil monetary penalty in an amount not to exceed 25 percent of the total value of the drug product lot or lots involved.

dimensions.assessment: Potential civil fine collections by the federal government, but overall economic impact is not fully quantified.
Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to add new labeling and supply chain transparency mandates.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require drug labeling to include original manufacturer and supply chain information.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory labeling requirements taking effect five years after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by this Act shall apply to active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished drug products that are manufactured and packaged on or after the date that is 5 years after the date of enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Aggregate financial compliance costs for the pharmaceutical industry are not estimated.
importance_detail.rationale: Requires active pharmaceutical ingredients and finished drug products to include original manufacturer and supply chain labeling information, backed by civil penalties from the FDA.
